title: Keylegend device profile
description: Describes one keyboard model in one physical layout: where every key sits, and which cell of the vendor LED matrix lights it. Adding a keyboard to Keylegend means writing one of these — never changing the program.

$schema.description: Points an editor at this file, so it can offer completion and flag mistakes while you type.

formatVersion.description: Revision of this format. Currently 1. A build refuses a profile numbered higher than it understands.

name.description: What the interface shows, e.g. "Razer DeathStalker V2".

vendor.description: Who makes the keyboard. "Generic" for a profile that describes a layout rather than a model.

model.description: The model, as the vendor writes it.

physicalLayout.description: The physical key arrangement, NOT the software layout: ANSI-US, ISO-DE, ISO-FR, JIS-JP, ABNT2-BR and so on. It decides the shape of the Enter key and whether the extra ISO keys exist. Which characters those keys produce is asked from Windows at runtime, so one profile serves every software layout on the same hardware.

image.description: Optional file name of a picture next to the profile. Currently unused — the preview is drawn from the geometry below. Only attach a picture you took or made yourself: everything here ships under the MIT licence, and a vendor's product render cannot.

usb.description: The USB identity of the keyboard, which is what lets it be recognised rather than guessed. Windows reports the same pair for attached hardware. Find yours with: Get-PnpDevice -Class Keyboard — the instance id contains VID_1532 and PID_0295. A vendor uses one product id across layouts, so a match narrows the choice to a model; the ISO or ANSI variant is then decided from the active Windows keyboard layout.

note.description: Free text for whoever opens the file next: what is still unchecked, which model it was written against, what surprised the person who calibrated it.

canvas.description: The coordinate system every key position refers to. Only ratios matter — the preview scales the whole thing to the room it has.

matrix.description: Size of the vendor LED matrix. Razer keyboards are 6 rows by 22 columns, whatever their size — a compact keyboard simply populates fewer cells.

verified.description: True only once somebody has stepped through the calibration on the real keyboard and confirmed that every key lights where the profile says. Geometry can be derived; this cannot.

id.description: Unique within the profile. Names follow the US layout by convention, so on a German keyboard the physical Z is Keyboard_Y. That is naming only — the character is queried from Windows.

row.description: Matrix row, or null while the mapping is unknown. Both row and column must be given, or neither.

column.description: Matrix column, or null while the mapping is unknown.

scanCode.description: Overrides the standard scan code for this key. Needed where the physical layout disagrees with the US-based naming — the tall ISO Enter, or a key that exists only on JIS or ABNT-2. Extended keys carry 0xE0 in the high byte.

parts.description: Further rectangles belonging to the same key, for keys that are not rectangular. The ISO Enter is the standard case: one key, two areas.

label.description: What is printed on the key, for keys that type nothing — strg, entf, pos 1. It belongs to the keyboard, not to the language of the software: a German keyboard says "Strg" whatever Keylegend is set to. Keys that produce a character need no label.

labelSecondary.description: A second line printed below the first — "s-abf" under "druck", or the navigation name under a number pad digit.
